evidence.title: Gordonia lasianthus
evidence.text: Gordonia lasianthus (loblolly-bay, holly-bay, gordonia, or bay) is a small to medium-sized evergreen tree or shrub found in acid, swampy soils of pinelands and bays on the Atlantic and Gulf Coastal Plains of the southeastern United States.

evidence.title: Gordonia lasianthus
evidence.text: It is a member of the Tea or Theaceae family.

evidence.title: Gordonia lasianthus
evidence.text: It is slow growing with soft, light-colored(Varies in color from Cream to Carmine), fine-grained wood of little commercial value, although loblolly-bay could be managed as a source of pulpwood.

evidence.title: Gordonia lasianthus

evidence.title: Gordonia lasianthus

evidence.title: Gordonia lasianthus
evidence.text: The bark of the adult tree varies from medium grey to a red brown coloration.

evidence.title: Gordonia lasianthus
evidence.text: Dead adult specimens of loblolly bay exhibit a lustorous shine when exposed to sunlight for several years.

evidence.title: Gordonia lasianthus
evidence.text: The white showy flowers and shiny foliage make it a desirable ornamental, but it is not easy to cultivate.

evidence.title: Osbeckia aspera

evidence.title: Osbeckia aspera
evidence.text: It is native to India and Sri Lanka.

evidence.title: Osbeckia aspera
evidence.text: Leaves are elliptic-lanceolate, base attenuate with more or less velvet-hairy on both sides.

evidence.title: Osbeckia aspera
evidence.text: Flowers are pink in color, show terminal cymes inflorescence.

evidence.title: Osbeckia aspera
evidence.text: Fruits are single seeded capsule.
